The original [SASRec sampler](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/sampler.py) excludes each user’s complete training-item set. Recommended implementation: exclude padding, the target, and all known training positives; retain repeated target occurrences as separate supervised positions. Sample 32 distinct negatives per position using batched uniform rejection sampling with duplicate rejection; chunk positions to bound memory. For dense histories, sample from an explicit eligible-item complement. Uniform weights with [`torch.multinomial(..., replacement=False)`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.multinomial.html) provide sampling without replacement, but avoid allocating position-by-catalog weight matrices. If fewer than 32 eligible items exist, use all eligible items and mask unused logits to −∞; report this exception. Skip positions with zero eligible negatives.

At example construction, preserve user IDs/full-history exclusion sets internally while keeping the public `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` interface, for example by generating negatives before discarding IDs. If resampling downstream, explicitly carry aligned history metadata through a custom loader mechanism. Truncated sequences cannot reliably identify users: identical sequence/target tuples can belong to different histories, so reverse lookup is ambiguous. For valid positions, construct `[positive_score, negative_scores] / temperature`, with finite temperature > 0, and call [`F.cross_entropy`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.CrossEntropyLoss.html) using zero-valued integer targets. Average over valid positions, not padded positions or candidate count; handle empty batches explicitly. Start with temperature 1 and tune separately.

Use a 2×2 comparison: BCE/CE × 1/32 negatives, holding architecture, sampling exclusions, training steps, seeds, and validation protocol fixed. Pair candidate draws across objectives. Explicitly define BCE scaling—e.g., positive loss plus mean negative loss per position—because summing negatives changes gradient scale with count. Report learning-rate/temperature tuning and wall-clock cost separately.
